name: Nature Sounds Through a Landline (Ahmed et al. 2025): degraded sounds, n-back and restoration
description:
Faithful replication of Ahmed, Van Hedger, Berman & Van Hedger (2025), "Listening through a landline: Using degraded sounds to examine the relationship between cognitive restoration and preference", Journal of Environmental Psychology 104, 102608 (doi:10.1016/j.jenvp.2025.102608; preprint "Perceptually degraded experiences with nature are liked less but still restorative", PsyArXiv knvy8). Rebuilt from the authors' own jsPsych script, instructions and sounds on OSF 5urta (osf.io/5urta). The OSF project gives no licence; the materials are used with credit and the template will be taken down if the authors object.

What participants do (about 40 minutes, computer with keyboard, headphones recommended): consent; volume calibration with a 5-s noise and the 6-trial Woods et al. (2017) headphone check; auditory n-back with spoken letters every 2.5 s (1-back practice, then 2-back ×2 and 3-back ×2; ← = match, → = no match; 10 targets and 20 non-targets per run) and a fatigue rating (1–5); five mood sliders (happy, sad, calm, anxious, lonely, 0–100, one per screen); an unannounced spoken attention check ("car"); random assignment to one of four sets of 40 fourteen-second recordings: unaltered nature (N01), degraded nature (N02, 400–2500 Hz band-pass like a landline phone), unaltered urban (U01) or degraded urban (U02); after each recording they rate liking, sound quality and urban-vs-natural (1–5, number keys or buttons); then mood sliders, n-back and fatigue again; Perceived Restorativeness Scale (9 items + attention item "moderately") and Mental Bandwidth Scale (7 items + attention item "extremely") about the sounds; optional age, gender, education, hearing aid, health issues and a guess of the study's purpose; debriefing.

Data: sound_ratings is keyed by recording (e.g. N02_17; the same number is the same recording unaltered/degraded). nback_pre / nback_post keep every letter, response and RT plus a summary with hits, false alarms, timeouts and d′ per level computed as in the authors' R script (log-linear correction, two runs pooled) and the share of letters answered. Analysis as in the paper: exclude failed attention checks (auditory, PRS_ATTN ≠ 3, MBS_ATTN ≠ 5), hearing-aid users and people who answered < 75 % of n-back letters; 2 (environment) × 2 (quality) ANOVAs on mean liking, quality and naturalness; ANCOVAs on post − pre change in 2-back/3-back d′ and fatigue with the pre score as covariate (with and without liking and affect change as covariates); MANOVA on PRS and MBS subscales.

Differences from the original study: (1) runs on SP-Survey instead of jsPsych 6.3 (same order, timing, wording and stimuli); (2) n-back letters converted from WAV to MP3 for the media library; (3) on-screen buttons are added next to the arrow and number keys so touch screens also work; (4) only the auditory attention check used in the shared script (attn1, "car") is included; the second check described in the paper (attn2.mp3) is left out because its answer words are not in the materials; (5) the Letter of Information and consent PDFs are summarised on the first page, there is no MTurk completion code, and the debriefing is shortened from the authors' letter; (6) PRS and MBS answers are stored as 1–5 (the jsPsych data used 0–4).
author: Ahmed, Van Hedger, Berman & Van Hedger

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I have read the Letter of Information, have had the nature of the study explained to me, and I agree to participate.

elements.name: headphone
elements.title: Volume calibration and headphone check
elements.description: { volume_plays, trials: [{ file, correct, answer, ok }], score } — Woods et al. (2017) loudness task, 6 trials in random order: which of three 200-Hz tones was quietest (one is in anti-phase). score 5–6 = likely headphones (not required).

elements.name: nback_pre
elements.title: Auditory n-back (before)
elements.description: { runs: [{ n, letters, types, resp, rt }], summary } — auditory n-back as in the authors' jsPsych script: runs 1-back (practice), 2, 2, 3, 3-back; each run has n lead-in letters then 10 targets and 20 non-targets in random order, one spoken letter every 2500 ms; ← = match, → = no match. types F/T/NT, resp 'L' | 'R' | null (no key), rt in ms from letter onset. summary: hits, false alarms, misses, correct rejections and timeouts per level, d′ per level with the log-linear correction used in the paper's R script (psycho::dprime adjusted, 2 runs pooled = 20 targets / 40 non-targets), and responded = share of scored letters with any key (the authors excluded < 75 %).

elements.name: fatigue_pre
elements.title: How fatigued are you feeling in the present moment?

choices.text: Very slightly or not at all

elements.name: vas_pre
elements.title: Mood (before)
elements.description: { happy, sad, calm, anxious, lonely } on 0–100 sliders (Not at all … Extremely), one term per screen in random order. Positive affect = mean of happy and calm; negative affect = mean of sad and anxious (post − pre).

elements.name: attn_audio
elements.title: Auditory attention check
elements.description: { answer, ok, rt } — an unannounced spoken prompt (attn1.mp3) asks to click one of five words (candle, club, car, carrot, candy); correct = car; 10-s limit (answer null when it runs out).

elements.name: listening
elements.title: Sound condition
elements.description: { condition: 'NAT_REG' | 'NAT_MAN' | 'URB_REG' | 'URB_MAN', environment: 'nature' | 'urban', quality: 'unaltered' | 'degraded', order, minutes } — random assignment to one of the four folders (N01 unaltered nature, N02 degraded nature, U01 unaltered urban, U02 degraded urban; degraded = 400–2500 Hz band-pass).

elements.name: sound_ratings
elements.title: Ratings of each 14-second recording

dimensions.label: How much did you like the sound you just heard?
Please rate the sound quality of the recording you just heard.
To what extent did the recording convey an urban (versus natural) setting?

elements.description: 40 recordings of the assigned folder, each once in random order; after each: like, sound quality, urban vs natural (1–5, keys or buttons). key = file name without .mp3 (e.g. N02_17; the same number is the same recording in N01/N02 and in U01/U02). 2 × 2 ANOVAs (environment × quality) on the participant means.

elements.name: vas_post
elements.title: Mood (after)
elements.description: Same five sliders after the sounds.

elements.name: nback_post
elements.title: Auditory n-back (after)
elements.description: Same task again. Main outcome: post − pre change in 2-back and 3-back d′ and in fatigue, 2 × 2 ANCOVA with the pre score as covariate.

elements.name: fatigue_post
elements.title: How fatigued are you feeling in the present moment?

choices.text: Very slightly or not at all

elements.name: prs

rows.text: Listening to these sounds helped me get away from it all.
Listening to these sounds was an escape for me.
Listening to these sounds helped me get relief from unwanted demands on my attention.
These sounds had qualities that drew me further in.
Once each sound started, I easily got pulled in.
While listening to the sounds, my attention was drawn to many interesting things.
The sounds had many fascinating qualities.
Listening to these sounds was a captivating experience.

elements.title: Please make your responses in reference to the longer sounds you rated in the middle of the study.

columns.text: very slightly or not at all

elements.description: Perceived Restorativeness Scale, 9 items (being away A, extent E, fascination F) + attention item PRS_ATTN (pass = 3, 'moderately'); 1–5 here (the jsPsych data stored 0–4). Items in random order.

elements.name: mbs

rows.text: While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you aware of the things going on around you?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you able to take note of your thoughts and feelings?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you lost in thought?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you letting your mind wander?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you thinking about the things you need to do?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you making plans for the future?
While listening to the sounds, to what degree were you reflecting on things that happened in the past?

elements.description: Mental Bandwidth Scale, 7 items (self-awareness SA, daydreaming D, planning P) + attention item MBS_ATTN (pass = 5, 'extremely'); 1–5. PRS and MBS: 2 × 2 MANOVA. Items in random order.

config.description: Faithful replication of Ahmed, Van Hedger, Berman & Van Hedger (2025), Journal of Environmental Psychology 104:102608, rebuilt from the authors' own jsPsych script and sounds (OSF 5urta). Participants calibrate volume and do a headphone check, then an auditory n-back (2- and 3-back), a fatigue rating and five mood sliders; they are randomly assigned to listen to 40 fourteen-second recordings that are nature or urban and unaltered or degraded (band-pass filtered like a landline telephone), rating each for liking, sound quality and naturalness; then mood, n-back and fatigue again, the Perceived Restorativeness Scale, the Mental Bandwidth Scale and demographics.
